tldr: For observational binary outcomes with arbitrary masses on \(d\) confounder categories and one-quarter overlap, the central pure-private minimax ATE MSE is \(\min\{1,n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2(e+d\rho)]+(n\rho)^{-2}\}\). An explicit evaluable release combines a clipped factorial-polynomial light branch, a pilot-capped regularized heavy branch, calibrated vector Laplace noise, and a rate-correct fallback. The matching converse constructs normalized legal causal priors and transports a moment-matched Poisson coupling through extraction of exactly \(n\) records. The observed marginals generated by \(\mathcal P_d\) coincide, modulo irrelevant values on zero-mass categories, with the one-quarter-overlap observed class used by Zeng--Balakrishnan--Han--Kennedy; conversely each such observed law has a consistency-and-exchangeability full-data extension. Their displayed Theorem 2 is for \(\psi_1\), they state the analogous nonprivate ATE lower rate, and they do not provide the matching polynomial upper estimator.
gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 provides published nonprivate lower-bound substrate: Theorem 2 is displayed for \(\psi_1\), the paper states the analogous ATE lower-rate conclusion, and it leaves construction of an attaining polynomial estimator to future work. A matching nonprivate upper construction exists only in the accepted internal non-archival substrate. Central-private causal papers isolate algorithmic sensitivity or a one-dimensional private-mean floor, but they do not determine whether privacy changes the logarithmic gain from polynomial estimation of rare confounding cells.
fill: The explicit fallback, capped hybrid, and expected-edit moment game target a single matched frontier and its sampling, sparse-cell, and direct-privacy phases; the full theorem remains conditional on the stated cap-MSE question.
